mission_07: Task embeddings represent entire tasks as fixed-dimensional vectors, enabling comparison, clustering, and retrieval of tasks based on their characteristics. A task embedding captures the essential properties of a learning problem — the data distribution, class structure, difficulty, and other meta-features. Common approaches include: (1) statistical embeddings using class means, variances, and covariances; (2) gradient-based embeddings using the direction and magnitude of gradients on the support set; (3) learned embeddings using a neural network that processes the support set. Task embeddings enable several powerful applications: task clustering groups similar tasks for multi-task learning, task retrieval finds relevant source tasks for transfer learning, and task-aware model selection chooses the best pre-trained model for a new task. Understanding task similarity is crucial for building systems that can automatically adapt their learning strategy based on the characteristics of the incoming task.
